summary: 44-year-old woman, day 1 after uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy: T 38.2°C, HR 94, reduced basal air entry, clean wounds.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Temperature on the ward the day after surgery
inputs.hpi: Day 1 after uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy (kept in for nausea). Temperature 38.2°C this morning. Shallow breathing because of port-site pain. Tolerating fluids, passing urine, mobilised to the bathroom. No rigors, no cough, no calf pain.

exam.general: Comfortable. HR 94, BP 124/76, RR 18, SpO2 95% on air, T 38.2°C.
exam.respiratory: Reduced air entry at both bases, no bronchial breathing.
exam.abdomen: Port sites clean and dry. Soft, appropriately tender around the port sites.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Early post-operative pyrexia (day 1) — probable basal atelectasis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Day 1 post-operative pyrexia 38.2°C, haemodynamically normal, basal atelectasis likely; wounds clean. Chest physiotherapy, analgesia, mobilise; no antibiotics; reassess.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy: acute cholecystitis, acute cholangitis, liver abscess. Nothing reads the surgical history, so the removed gallbladder ranks first; no atelectasis/pneumonia node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: condition on surgical history (no gallbladder diagnoses after cholecystectomy, no appendicitis after appendicectomy) and add early post-operative causes.

emergencyLevel.note: A well patient with a day-1 fever needs clinical review, not an emergency response.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage emergency_now (score 152) for T 38.2, HR 94 on day 1: 'Post-operative concern' (urgent) for any 'post-op' word, 'Post-op fever — source must be identified', 'Fever', and the anticoagulant reason (prophylactic enoxaparin).
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Post-operative ward reviews: score post-op concern from physiology (NEWS2) rather than adding 'Post-operative concern' (urgent) for any 'post-op'/'wound' word; reserve emergency_now for physiological or peritonitic criteria.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No chest physiotherapy/mobilisation/wound review line; the Assessment panel shows the cholecystitis protocol (PANE top).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Post-operative fever prompt by day (early: atelectasis/inflammatory; day 5+: leak/SSI/collection; UTI, line, VTE).

mustExclude.note: No broad-spectrum antibiotics for a day-1 fever without a source.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Assessment panel (cholecystitis protocol from PANE top): '[immediate] IV antibiotics: co-amoxiclav 1.2 g TDS or piperacillin-tazobactam for severe' for a day-1 fever after cholecystectomy.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Assessment panel: follow the locked working diagnosis, not the PANE top (findings/hpb.md gap 7).

mustExclude.note: The patient is on prophylactic-dose enoxaparin only; a peri-operative anticoagulant bridging plan does not apply.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Prophylactic enoxaparin 40 mg triggers anticoag_check ('Anticoagulation monitoring + peri-operative bridging plan', PT/INR, 'warfarin — bridge with LMWH'). It fires in all 10 post-operative vignettes whose only anticoagulant is standard prophylactic enoxaparin.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Replace the anticoag_check prompt in clinical-inference.ts with a rule table keyed on drug, indication and procedure bleeding risk (ACCP 2022 / BSG-ESGE 2021): warfarin — stop 5 days before, INR the day before, bridge only for mechanical mitral valve / recent VTE or stroke; DOAC — interrupt by drug, CrCl and bleeding risk, no bridging, no routine coagulation test; low-risk endoscopy — continue. Do not fire it for prophylactic-dose LMWH.

mustExclude.note: No generalised peritonitis or perforation: an emergency-laparotomy consent line is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ACCM/IDSA — evaluation of new fever in critically ill adult patients (2008 update)
guideline.section: Fever in the first 48 h after surgery is usually non-infectious; evaluate clinically (chest, wound, lines, urine) before investigating or starting antibiotics
guideline.citation: O'Grady NP, Barie PS, Bartlett JG, et al. Crit Care Med. 2008;36:1330–49.

guideline.name: RCP — National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
guideline.section: Aggregate ≥7: emergency response — urgent assessment by a team with critical-care competencies, continuous monitoring; 5–6 or a single red parameter: urgent response
guideline.citation: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2. London: RCP; 2017.

guideline.name: NICE NG89 — Venous thromboembolism in over 16s: reducing the risk of hospital-acquired DVT or PE
guideline.section: Assess VTE and bleeding risk; abdominal surgery with VTE risk above bleeding risk: pharmacological prophylaxis (LMWH) for at least 7 days; extended to 28 days after major cancer surgery in the abdomen/pelvis; mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or IPC) when pharmacological prophylaxis is contraindicated by bleeding risk; reassess within 24 h and when the clinical situation changes
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. VTE in over 16s (NG89). London: NICE; 2018 (updated 2019).

rationale: Base post-operative fever case: early, non-infective. Tests over-triage and over-treatment. Every other post-operative complication vignette permutes this one.
